Cobra Presenting at Australia's Largest Copper Conference

Cobra (LSE: COBR), a South Australian mineral exploration and development company, announces its Managing Director and CEO Rupert Verco will be delivering a Spotlight Presentation on the Manna Hill Copper Project at this week's Copper to the World conference in Adelaide.

Copper to the World, Australia's largest copper conference, is being held in partnership with the Government of South Australia and seeks to position the state as the primary contributor to Australia becoming the world's third-largest copper producer by 2030, aiming to more than triple South Australia's copper production to a 1 million tonnes per annum.

As major copper discoveries are becoming less common and getting deeper, Cobra aims to contribute to this goal through its fertile landholding at Manna Hill with multiple prospects containing shallow copper and gold mineralisation. Cobra's initial Reverse Circulation drilling at the Blue Rose discovery at Manna Hill in January 2026 supports economic scale, with shallow, thick and high-grade intersections. The Company anticipates results of deeper diamond drilling shortly.
The Copper to the World presentation at the event is available for shareholders to view on the Company's website at: https://investors.cobraplc.com/reports-presentations-circulars.

About Cobra
Cobra Resources is a South Australian critical minerals developer, advancing assets at all stages of the pre-production pathway.

In 2023, Cobra identified the Boland ionic rare earth discovery at its Wudinna Project in the Gawler Craton - Australia's only rare earth project suitable for in situ recovery (ISR) mining. ISR is a low-cost, low-disturbance extraction method that eliminates the need for excavation, positioning Boland to achieve bottom-quartile recovery costs.

In 2025, Cobra further expanded its portfolio by optioning (and subsequently acquiring) the Manna Hill Copper Project in the Nackara Arc, South Australia. The project contains multiple underexplored prospects with strong potential to deliver large-scale copper discoveries.
In 2025, Cobra sold its Wudinna Gold Assets to Barton Gold (ASX: BDG) for up to A$15 million in cash and shares.
